evidence_packet.title: Wigan Council renames town square in honour of Sir Billy Boston
evidence_packet.lead: Sir Billy Boston was "a pioneer" and "an inspiration" and his legacy will continue, Wigan Council says
evidence_packet.summary: Sir Billy Boston was "a pioneer" and "an inspiration" and his legacy will continue, Wigan Council says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council renames town square in honour of Sir Billy Boston - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Sir Billy Boston already has a statue and a plaque in the square now named after him By Paul Burnell North West , Reporting from in Wigan Published 1 hour ago Rugby League star Sir Billy Boston is to be further honoured in his adopted hometown Wigan, with the renaming of the town's square where his statue is situated. Sir Billy, who was Rugby league's first knight, died last month, aged 92. His funeral took place at Wigan Warriors' Brick Community Stadium on Thursday. Believe Square will now be called Sir Billy Boston Square "to ensure his legacy continues" in the heart of the town, Wigan Council has announced. In March, a civic service was held to mark a new plaque being added to his statue, following his knighthood in 2025. 'An inspiration' Born in Cardiff in 1934, Sir Billy grew up playing rugby union but faced prejudice because of his ethnicity and was overlooked by his home club. He came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old. Wigan Council leader Nazia Rehman said Sir Billy was "more than a sporting legend, he was a pioneer, an inspiration, and someone who brought immense pride to Wigan Borough". Image caption, The statue of Sir Billy Boston in Believe Square, Wigan, was unveiled in 2016 Rehman said: "Following his passing, we wanted to ensure his legacy continues to be honoured in the heart of our town. "That's why we are renaming Believe Square, the home of Sir Billy's statue, as Sir Billy Boston Square." evidence_packet.summary: Thomas White has been transferred from a secure psychiatric hospital back to prison, his family say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Family's fears for Thomas White as he is sent back to jail - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Clara White (right), pictured with Thomas White and his mother, said she was calling for the government to establish a clear timeline and plan to resolve the IPP injustice By Angela Ferguson North West Published 10 September 2026 The family of a man serving an indefinite prison sentence say they fear for his health after he was transferred back to jail from a secure psychiatric hospital. Thomas White, 43, was given an Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence for stealing a mobile phone in 2012. The sentences, which have no fixed release date, were abolished four months later. His sister, Clara White, said he was "a severely unwell man who needs treatment, stability and hope". The Ministry of Justice has been approached for comment. Clara said the family "felt a small sense of hope" when White was moved from HMP Manchester to a secure psychiatric hospital, but now say "he is being sent back into the very system that made him ill". She said her brother, who has a teenage son, had already been moved between 14 prisons and that this latest transfer would make it his 15th in 14 years. While he needed treatment and support, he was instead being "sent back to prison with no release date and no certainty about what his future holds", she said. White had been binge-drinking in Manchester before he stole a phone from two Christian missionaries in 2012. He was given an IPP sentence with a minimum tariff of two years. His family said he has now spent more than 14 years in custody, serving more than seven times that period. title: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme

evidence_packet.title: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme
evidence_packet.lead: The walkways will connect parts of Manchester city centre to other places, including the Etihad campus
evidence_packet.summary: The walkways will connect parts of Manchester city centre to other places, including the Etihad campus
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme - BBC News Image caption, The CyanLines project will see a number of "floating walkways" connecting different parts of Manchester By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 10 September 2026 Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed. It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade. The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." There are two further CyanLines routes in development in Newton Heath and Rusholme. Backing for the plans comes from the Manchester and Trafford councils, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City FC, the Canal and River Trust, property developers Renaker and Urban Splash, and the National Trust, among others. Pete Bradshaw, director of sustainability at Manchester City, said: "The plans for the CyanLines route add a new layer of nature-rich, innovative and imaginative active travel and community experiences for fans, visitors and those living and working in the neighbourhood." Image caption, The next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct park project has also been announced Funding for the next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct "garden in the sky" was also announced. Part of the old railway line has been transformed into a public park, which opened in 2022.

title: Woman who falsely accused 10 men of rape has jail term increased

evidence_packet.title: Woman who falsely accused 10 men of rape has jail term increased
evidence_packet.lead: Stacey Sharples, who falsely accused 10 men of rape, has her sentence increased to seven years
evidence_packet.summary: Stacey Sharples, who falsely accused 10 men of rape, has her sentence increased to seven years
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after the Court of Appeal ruled her original term was "unduly lenient" Stacey Sharples, 31, made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and relationships, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019, when she was aged between 18 and 24 Sharples, who admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice, was originally jailed for four-and-a-half years, but judges increased the term to seven years The Attorney General had referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal, after Sharples was jailed at Bolton Crown Court in March An estimated 264 hours of police time and about £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after the Court of Appeal ruled her original term was "unduly lenient" Stacey Sharples, 31, made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and relationships, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019, when she was aged between 18 and 24 Sharples, who admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice, was originally jailed for four-and-a-half years, but judges increased the term to seven years The Attorney General had referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal, after Sharples was jailed at Bolton Crown Court in March An estimated 264 hours of police time and about £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trains Faster trains, battery power, more jobs, as Andy Burnham announces £1bn plan for the north "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came" News Sophie Wingate, PA and Stephen Topping Se Andy Burnham has announced a £1 billion investment which should bring faster and 'more reliable' trains to Manchester and the north A new TransPennine Express fleet of 29 battery-electric trains will cut journey times by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds, and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York, the government says The new trains will run on routes between Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull. They should be built from 2028 and enter service from the end of 2034 The Prime Minister said: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came. And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities "Today that starts to change. These 29 new trains will bring faster, more reliable journeys to the North, and thousands of British jobs for the next generation. It's exactly what Great British Railways is all about - taking back control of the basics and getting Britain believing

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 Arsonists were caught on CCTV breaking into a business and starting a fire while one of them was still inside. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. The third man, who was behind the shutters, was seen on CCTV fleeing like a 'scalded cat', appearing to be on fire After the flames died down, he joined the other two in the car before it sped off. Firefigthers raced to the scene and the blaze was extinguished. Around £300,000 of damage was caused at the bedding supply business

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 6 hours ago Burnage by-election RECAP as Labour HOLD mayor Bev Craig's former council seat in fight against Greens Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour in a close and crucial by-election A smiling Carl Austi Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour, beating his main rival, Green Party's Daoud Nawaz The race was tipped as a ‘huge’ moment for the city’s future with the Greens gunning to make a ‘statement’ by taking the former council leader’s seat, which has boundaries covering Burnage and parts of southern Levenshulme The seat with nearly 14,000 voters was up for grabs after former Manchester City Council leader Ms Craig was elected as mayor of Greater Manchester in July While the outcome in Burnage tonight won’t have a drastic impact on the overall control of the council which is comfortably in Labour’s hands, it could be a sign of things to come with the May 2027 local elections now just eight months away Manchester council is run by the Labour Party, which holds 63 seats in the city, next to the opposition Greens with 21, seven Reform UK councillors, and four Lib Dems

evidence_packet.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Rural Bolton quarry due to close this year asks to extend operations until 2031 Harwood Quarry is only one of two in the country that can produce the shale needed to create high-quality bricks Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 14 A long-standing rural quarry is seeking to expend its operations for another five years Harwood Quarry, on the north east outskirts of Bolton , has seen shale extracted from the ground to make bricks for generations, but its licence is due to expire at the end of 2026 A planning application has been lodged to extend that period until 2031, due to what the company said was ‘cumulative commercial and practical factors, beyond its control’ Booth Ventures Ltd, which runs the site, said those reasons included disruption caused by the Covid pandemic, significant increases in energy and construction costs and difficulties within the regional and national construction sector The firm said that has affected its delivery programme and delayed its completion by the deadline of December 31, 2026

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trains Faster trains, battery power, more jobs, as Andy Burnham announces £1bn plan for the north "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came" News Sophie Wingate, PA and Stephen Topping Se Andy Burnham has announced a £1 billion investment which should bring faster and 'more reliable' trains to Manchester and the north A new TransPennine Express fleet of 29 battery-electric trains will cut journey times by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds, and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York, the government says The new trains will run on routes between Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull. They should be built from 2028 and enter service from the end of 2034 The Prime Minister said: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came. And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities "Today that starts to change. These 29 new trains will bring faster, more reliable journeys to the North, and thousands of British jobs for the next generation. It's exactly what Great British Railways is all about - taking back control of the basics and getting Britain believing

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury The plan to plug the gap between Bolton and Bury that won’t cost a penny The project has been described as 'crucial' Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:17, 11 Sep 2026 View Image The council hopes the project will create a ‘year-round’ route (Ima A project to create a new and improved cycle route between Bury town centre and Bolton has been unveiled The scheme will see existing off-road provision between Ainsworth Road and Bolton Road upgraded, offering cyclists a ‘safe alternative’ to the A58, Bury council has said. evidence_packet.summary: Wigan The site 'pivotal in shaping Wigan's future' Westwood Park has been described as 'a new gateway to Wigan town centre' News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Westwood Park (Image: Wigan council) A plan for one of Wigan’s largest development
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The site 'pivotal in shaping Wigan's future' Westwood Park has been described as 'a new gateway to Wigan town centre' News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Westwood Park (Image: Wigan council) A plan for one of Wigan’s largest development sites is out for public consultation over the next six weeks. Westwood Park, around a kilometre south of the town centre has been described as ‘pivotal in shaping the town’s future’ The borough’s draft local plan states the 58-acre brownfield site as being suitable for around 420 new homes and modern employment space The huge plot is previously developed as it was home to the Westwood power station, which closed in 1986 The site is bounded by the west coast mainline railway to the east, the A49 Westwood Way with the alignment of the proposed Wigan-Hindley link road and Westwood Lane to the south Westwood Flash is to the west with the Leeds-Liverpool canal and existing employment development to the north

evidence_packet.title: 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up
evidence_packet.lead: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou
evidence_packet.summary: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 Arsonists were caught on CCTV breaking into a business and starting a fire while one of them was still inside. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. The third man, who was behind the shutters, was seen on CCTV fleeing like a 'scalded cat', appearing to be on fire After the flames died down, he joined the other two in the car before it sped off. Firefigthers raced to the scene and the blaze was extinguished. Around £300,000 of damage was caused at the bedding supply business

title: Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference

evidence_packet.title: Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference
evidence_packet.lead: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage
evidence_packet.summary: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage by-election to hold onto former council leader Bev Craig’s old seat Councillor Carl Austin-Behan was elected on Thursday night (September 10) picking up 1,365 votes in a race which was expected to be ‘very close’ with the Greens. In the end Green Party candidate Daoud Nawaz got a total of 1,037 ballots The vote on September 10 was triggered back in July when Bev Craig was elected as Greater Manchester mayor, requiring her to stand down as a councillor in the Burnage ward and as leader of Manchester City Council New Burnage Councillor Carl Austin-Behan said he felt ‘honoured’ that residents had put their trust in him once again after previously being elected to the ward from 2011 to 2018 View 3 Images Daoud Nawaz came second for the Green Party (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News)

title: The Mancunian Way: What's happened to the Printworks?

evidence_packet.title: The Mancunian Way: What's happened to the Printworks?
evidence_packet.lead: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed.
evidence_packet.summary: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close
evidence_packet.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man appears in court to deny murdering Stretford Grammar School headteacher Simon Richardson is due to go on trial next month News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 11:15, 10 Sep 2026 View Image Michael Mullins (Image: MEN Media) A man has appeared in court to deny the murder of Stretford Grammar School headteacher Michael Mullins. Simon Richardson, 35, pleaded not guilty to murdering Mr Mullins. He died following an incident on April 20 this year Mr Richardson, of no fixed address, but formerly of Epsom Avenue in Sale, also pleaded not guilty to manslaughter and dangerous driving, by driving a Ford Transit van on roads including Williams Street, Oldham Road, Wellington Street, Peace Street, Wickentree Lane, Wrigley Head a He is due to go on trial next month at Minshull Street Crown Court. Emergency services were called to reports of a collision involving a car and a cyclist on Paddock Lane, in Dunham Massey near Altrincham, at around 6.10pm on April 20 The cyclist, Mr Mullins, 56, died at the scene. He had been headteacher of Stretford Grammar School for 17 years Judge Maurice Greene told Mr Richardson, who appeared in court by video link: “Your trial will be on October 13. There will be a pre-trial review, as things stand, on October 2. You will remain in custody.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Paul Dennett Salford postcode lottery fears as parents issued with £1m update ahead of school holidays Thousands of children could benefit from the decision made today but concerns remain about the impact of recent government changes Comments News Edw Salford council will look to lobby the government over fears an expansion of free school meals could become a ‘postcode lottery’ without more support. It comes as more than 16,000 children could benefit from support over the holidays At the council’s Cabinet meeting today (8 September), it was agreed to continue the city’s existing school holiday food support scheme for the October half-term, Christmas holidays and February half-term. Between now and 2029, the local authority will receive £6m The decision reallocate £1m to continue the scheme will provide eligible families with continued financial support during the remaining school holiday periods of the 2026/27 financial year, giving additional support at a time when the cost of feeding children can place extra pres Before the government expanded free school meals, there were nearly 16,000 children eligible across the borough in 2024. A 2026 cabinet report said there were 17,410 live claims and over a quarter of children in Salford were ;living in absolute low income families in 2023/24′ The move was broadly welcomed by cabinet members who praised the support provided against a backdrop of families struggling with the cost of living. Criticisms were also levelled over the current income threshold for free school meals for being too low

Oli Coppock, from Warrington , turned up to hospital with an overnight bag when he first felt unwell But the 34-year-old was sent home from Warrington Hospital and told to take paracetamol. The aspiring DJ and Manchester United fan went on to suffer a cardiac arrest Fluid on his brain was discovered at a later CT scan, and Oli was diagnosed with inoperable brain stem damage. Oli is now non-verbal - and his family have sued the NHS over the blunder Dad Stephen Coppock said: "Warrington [Hospital] should hold their heads in shame. As far as I am concerned, the health service that he trusted to protect him has destroyed my boy by failing to do the basics and his life was ruined at 32 now he is a shell of his former self "They robbed him of his life. evidence_packet.lead: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou
evidence_packet.summary: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 Arsonists were caught on CCTV breaking into a business and starting a fire while one of them was still inside. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. The third man, who was behind the shutters, was seen on CCTV fleeing like a 'scalded cat', appearing to be on fire After the flames died down, he joined the other two in the car before it sped off. Firefigthers raced to the scene and the blaze was extinguished. Around £300,000 of damage was caused at the bedding supply business

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 6 hours ago Burnage by-election RECAP as Labour HOLD mayor Bev Craig's former council seat in fight against Greens Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour in a close and crucial by-election A smiling Carl Austi Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour, beating his main rival, Green Party's Daoud Nawaz The race was tipped as a ‘huge’ moment for the city’s future with the Greens gunning to make a ‘statement’ by taking the former council leader’s seat, which has boundaries covering Burnage and parts of southern Levenshulme The seat with nearly 14,000 voters was up for grabs after former Manchester City Council leader Ms Craig was elected as mayor of Greater Manchester in July While the outcome in Burnage tonight won’t have a drastic impact on the overall control of the council which is comfortably in Labour’s hands, it could be a sign of things to come with the May 2027 local elections now just eight months away Manchester council is run by the Labour Party, which holds 63 seats in the city, next to the opposition Greens with 21, seven Reform UK councillors, and four Lib Dems

evidence_packet.lead: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage
evidence_packet.summary: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage by-election to hold onto former council leader Bev Craig’s old seat Councillor Carl Austin-Behan was elected on Thursday night (September 10) picking up 1,365 votes in a race which was expected to be ‘very close’ with the Greens. In the end Green Party candidate Daoud Nawaz got a total of 1,037 ballots The vote on September 10 was triggered back in July when Bev Craig was elected as Greater Manchester mayor, requiring her to stand down as a councillor in the Burnage ward and as leader of Manchester City Council New Burnage Councillor Carl Austin-Behan said he felt ‘honoured’ that residents had put their trust in him once again after previously being elected to the ward from 2011 to 2018 View 3 Images Daoud Nawaz came second for the Green Party (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News)

title: The Mancunian Way: What's happened to the Printworks?

evidence_packet.title: The Mancunian Way: What's happened to the Printworks?
evidence_packet.lead: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed.
evidence_packet.summary: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close
evidence_packet.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Whitefield 'You say brownfield sites come first. Absolutely not. There’s hectares and hectares of greenbelt you’re destroying' Plans for over-55s flats in Whitefield are met with scorn from public gallery Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:01, 10 Sep Bury council has revealed ambitions to build new homes on vacant land in Whitefield - but one member of the public gave a scornful objection to the council's 'brownfield first' boast The scheme, off Elms Close, is expected to create 16 affordable flats for residents over the age of 55, with the council saying this would promote independent living and help meet the needs of an ‘ageing population’. The site, known as The Elms, was previously home to a Victorian Bury council had planned to dispose of the site to a developer, but has now said it intends to carry out the project itself. This means it will have greater control over the final scheme and the new homes would be added to the council’s housing stock, generating new income for th The authority’s cabinet signed off on the move at a meeting last night. Lead member for regeneration and growth Charlotte Morris said the scheme is ‘in line’ with the council’s ‘ambitions and vision’ to deliver affordable homes and build on brownfield sites ‘first’ However, that pronouncement was met with scorn from some in the public gallery. One woman, whose name was just given as Amanda, interrupted the meeting to dispute the council’s ‘brownfield first’ claim

Emma Murray, 33, flew into a rage and threw the glass against a wall after accusing Allen Smith of being unreceptive when she was telling him something. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Long-term participation in pensions, savings and investing also shapes financial resilience, and those outcomes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester has a growing reputation for female entrepreneurship, technology and professional services, yet access to capital is only one part of the financial picture. Long-term participation in pensions, savings and investing also shapes financial resilience, and those outcomes Women are often described as less confident investors, but that explanation can overlook the wider conditions surrounding financial decisions. Income stability, time available for financial planning, workplace benefits and familiarity with investment terminology can all affect wh Initiatives such as Loud Investing challenge the idea that women simply need to become more confident before investing. A more useful approach treats confidence as something that can develop through knowledge, clearer information and experience rather than as a personality trait That distinction matters in a city where many women are building businesses, moving through fast-changing careers or balancing professional growth with family responsibilities Greater Manchester has developed a strong ecosystem of women-led businesses across technology, media, professional services and consumer sectors. Yet access to funding remains uneven Recent reporting on female founders raising investment in the North has highlighted the practical barriers some Manchester entrepreneurs continue to face, from limited investor networks to difficulties securing growth capital

McHale Group, which employs 152 people across five offices, passed the milestone in the year to May 31 and has now outlined plans for further expansion. The group is planning to open new offices in Manchester city centre and Cheshire over the next 12 months, while discussions over the acquisition of two other firms are said to be at an advanced stage. It is also expanding its Altrincham headquarters at Warrant House, where it has taken an additional 4,500 sq ft to accommodate the growth of its real estate team. Plans are already under way to take further space in the building. McHale & Co was founded by Andrew McHale in Levenshulme in 2001, initially specialising in criminal law before expanding into conveyancing. Over the subsequent 25 years, it has grown both organically and through acquisitions into a full-service legal group, with offices in Altrincham, Stockport, Heywood, London and Solihull. Andrew moved into the role of group chairman earlier this year, with Adam Horner and Kamil Tomaszewski taking over as joint chief executives. “It’s been a rollercoaster ride over the past 25 years, and I feel blessed that so many great people have been part of the journey,” said Andrew. title: Manchester toughens stance on fly-tipping with increase to fines

evidence_packet.title: Manchester toughens stance on fly-tipping with increase to fines
evidence_packet.lead: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount
evidence_packet.summary: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount Offenders caught committing fly-tipping offences will now face a £1,000 fine, an increase from the current £700 penalty. Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. A total of 992 fines were issued for waste deposits in the same period The strategy supports the aims of the council's Our Manchester Strategy , which sets out a vision for cleaner, greener and better maintained neighbourhoods

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. Download Bury Council's Trading Standards Service has carried out a major intelligence-led enforcement operation targeting the sale of illicit tobacco, illegal vaping products and other unlawful goods across the borough The operation follows the recent Council motion committing Bury to a zero-tolerance approach towards illegal tobacco and vape sales, in so-called 'dodgy shops'. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A shop in Leigh town centre has been closed for three months following repeated seizures of illicit tobacco products Wigan Council’s Trading Standards team, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police, secured the closure order for Shop & Save on Bradshawgate after concerns were raised about illegal sales Following an investigation by Trading Standards, a three-month closure order was approved at Wigan and Leigh Magistrates Court on Thursday, 3rd September Councillor Kevin Anderson, portfolio holder for police, crime and civil contingencies said: "This closure order yet again demonstrates our commitment to tackling illegal trading and protecting our communities across Wigan Borough “Traders who engage in this kind of activity will not be allowed to continue breaking the law, and we will continue working with partners to investigate reports of illicit sales and take robust action where unlawful activity is identified.” Over the course of two months, Trading Standards officers seized 7,380 sticks of illicit cigarettes and four kilograms of illicit hand rolling tobacco, which was concealed in elaborate hides within the premises

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Leisure centre memberships in Wigan Borough have reached never-before-seen heights as residents become more active A strong summer of sign-ups has seen the council-run Be Well brand surpass 20,000 members for the first time ever - suggesting local people are increasingly conscious of the importance of moving more Memberships are up by just shy of 2,000 this year alone and have close to doubled since the council’s decision to bring leisure services back in-house in 2021 Total visitor numbers across Be Well’s seven sites also continue to rise, putting them on course to top the 1.73million visits that were made by residents from April 2025 to March 2026 The impressive figures come on the back of major council investment in the borough’s leisure facilities, with recent refurbs bringing brand-new, state-of-the-art fitness equipment at all locations Councillor Chris Ready, Wigan Council’s cabinet portfolio holder for communities and neighbourhoods, believes a combination of cutting-edge facilities, an inclusive community, and an emphasis on holistic wellbeing over body image has been the secret to Be Well’s success

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Quays is Greater Manchester's unique waterfront destination, situated just 15 minutes by tram from Manchester city centre. It is Britain's hottest short-break destination and packs everything you can do in a big city into one spectacular square mile. Shopping, sport, art, dra Live theatre, the best of cinema and one of the country's finest museums: The Quays offers a fantastic choice of things to do and see. Imperial War Museum North and The Lowry are vibrant and exciting examples of contemporary architecture, the contents as stunning as the setting a Whether you're a shopaholic or just someone who likes a bargain, the opening of the Quayside MediaCityUK has made The Quays a mecca for the discerning shopper with big-name brand shops and stores offering discount prices - up to 70 per cent lower than the high street - all year r There's no better place to find top sport action than The Quays. Home to two of the most renowned clubs in British sport - Manchester United and Lancashire County Cricket Club , The Quays is the area to head for when wanting the best in football and cricket. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Our Mayor is now our Prime Minister, and the skills agenda he's brought to Downing Street is one we've lived and breathed for over a decade Andy Burnham has spent some of his first fortnight in office setting out plans to reshape technical education and get more young people into work, built on the MBacc model developed here in Greater Manchester. This is familiar ground for us. For over ten years Manchester Digital That gap has become harder to bridge, economic uncertainty, higher costs and cautious hiring are playing their part as is AI, which is starting to strip out the routine tasks junior roles were built on. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Why two Manchester United substitutes left Michael Carrick "delighted" vs Sabah Man Utd beat Sabah 4-0 in the Champions League, and the manner of the win allowed Michael Carrick to use all five substitutes with time to spare.
